name: Airtable
description: Airtable is a cloud platform that combines a relational database with spreadsheet-like views, letting teams build custom apps, automations, and interfaces on top of their own data without traditional coding.
best_for: Positioned for teams in product, marketing, project management, operations, sales, design, HR, and finance who want to move off spreadsheets toward custom interfaces and automations.
features: Relational database foundation shared across a team
Multiple customizable views for the same underlying data
Interface Designer for building custom drag-and-drop apps

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: 1,000 records per base, up to 5 editors, 1 GB of attachments per base, 100 automation runs.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.notes: Per seat/month, billed annually. 50,000 records per base, 20 GB attachments per base, 25,000 automation runs.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: Per seat/month, billed annually. 125,000 records per base, 100 GB attachments, SAML SSO, admin panel.

tiers.name: Enterprise Scale
tiers.notes: Contact sales. 500,000 records per base, 1,000 GB attachments, enterprise API, audit logs.

cons: Every plan caps records and attachment storage per base, not per account -- once a base hits its limit (1,000 records on Free), you can't add more records or attachments until you upgrade.
The Free plan caps out at 5 editors, so team growth past that forces a paid tier even before hitting record limits.

alternatives.name: Notion
alternatives.description: An all-in-one workspace combining documents, databases, project tracking, and team knowledge.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want databases alongside docs and wikis in one workspace

alternatives.name: ClickUp

alternatives.best_for: Teams that want project management more than database structure

alternatives.name: Monday.com

alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting a more visual, board-first workflow
